# Bracelet Try-ON — Agent Guide

_Reach for this app when a bracelet product photo needs to be shown worn on a model's wrist — for listings, social posts, or lookbooks._

## What it does — and what it will NOT do

**Does:** Places a bracelet from a product photo onto a model's wrist. The model is generated by the app, or styled after an optional reference photo. Handles every bracelet type: bangles, chain bracelets, cuffs, tennis bracelets, charm bracelets. Output is either a clean in-studio white background (`is_lifestyle` false, the default) or a lifestyle scene (`is_lifestyle` true), framed either as a wrist close-up (`is_closeup` true) or a wider shot (false, the default).

**Will NOT do:**
- Watches — not even fitness bands without a time display.
- Other jewelry types (rings, earrings, necklaces) or several jewelry types in one run.
- Retouching, polishing, or quality enhancement — the bracelet is placed exactly as it appears in the photo, flaws included.
- Design changes — metal swap, charm changes, length changes.
- Exact preservation of the model reference. `model_input` is a **style reference only**; the generated person will differ. Do not promise a specific person's likeness.

## Choose it / don't choose it

| Situation | Use instead |
|---|---|
| The piece is a watch or fitness band | **Watch Try-On** |
| The piece is a ring | **Rings Try On** |
| The piece is earrings | **Earrings Try On** |
| The piece is a necklace or pendant | **Necklace Try - On** |
| Multiple jewelry types worn together in one image | **Jewelry Set Try-On** |
| The bracelet photo needs cleanup first (scratches, dull metal, soft detail) | **Jewelry Retoucher Vivid** first, then this app with the retouched image URL |
| The bracelet's design must change (metal, charms, length) | **Jewelry Modifier Pro** first, then this app with the modified image URL |

## Inputs that make or break the result

- `jewelry_photo_1` (required): a publicly reachable HTTPS URL of a **clean product shot on a plain background**, bracelet clearly visible. A photo of the bracelet already being worn can work — the app tries to extract the piece — but results vary; a flat product photo is more reliable.
- **Fill the frame.** If the bracelet is small with lots of empty background, fine details get lost. Crop the image closer to the bracelet before hosting it and pass the cropped version's URL.
- **Sharpness in = sharpness out.** A soft source still runs, but fine links, pavé, and engraving detail will be lost. Retouch or provide a higher-quality photo for crisp results.
- **Multiple bracelets in one photo are ambiguous.** Either crop to the single bracelet wanted, or disambiguate in `user_instructions` ("use the bracelet on the left" / "these are two separate pieces — stack both together on the wrist"). Without this, pieces can be merged into one invented design.
- `model_input` (optional): if used, pick a reference whose **placement wrist is bare and visible** — no watch, no existing bracelets, no sleeve covering the wrist. Some wrist skin must be visible for correct placement. Otherwise omit it and let the app generate the model.
- **Match the framing flags to the reference.** A wide-shot reference with `is_closeup: true` yields a wrist-only crop that won't resemble the reference; a wrist-close-up reference with `is_closeup: false` means most of the model is generated. Likewise `is_lifestyle` should agree with whether the reference is a lifestyle scene or a studio shot — mismatches produce backgrounds the user didn't expect.
- **Keep `user_instructions`, `product_size`, and the flags mutually consistent.** Instructions describing a wide shot while `is_closeup` is true (or vice versa), or a size selection contradicting the described bracelet, produce confused results.

## Parameter playbook

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Values / range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jewelry_photo_1` | image_url | yes | — | public HTTPS URL of the bracelet |
| `product_size` | string | no | `M (Medium)` | `XS (Extra Small)`, `S (Small)`, `M (Medium)`, `L (Large)`, `XL (Extra Large)` |
| `model_input` | image_url | no | — | model reference (style only, not preserved) |
| `gender` | string | no | `female` | `female`, `male` |
| `is_lifestyle` | boolean | no | `false` | `true` = lifestyle scene (describe it in instructions); `false` = studio white background |
| `is_closeup` | boolean | no | `false` | `true` = wrist-area framing; `false` = wider shot |
| `model_tier` | string | no | `ViTryon SD - 1Mpx` | `ViTryon SD - 1Mpx`, `ViTryon PRO (HQ) - 4Mpx`, `ViTryon PRO (HQ) - 16Mpx` — HQ tiers are more precise and render up to 16Mpx natively |
| `user_instructions` | string (multiline) | no | `""` | free text, any language |
| `aspect_ratio` | string | no | `auto` | `auto`, `1:1`, `1:4`, `1:8`, `2:3`, `3:2`, `3:4`, `4:1`, `4:3`, `4:5`, `5:4`, `8:1`, `9:16`, `16:9`, `21:9` (`auto` matches the bracelet crop) |
| `extension` | string | no | `png` | `png`, `jpg`, `webp` |
| `quality` | integer | no | `80` | 50–100 (JPEG only) |
| `lossless_webp` | string | no | `"true"` | `"false"`, `"true"` (string enum, not boolean) |
| `dpi` | integer | no | `300` | 72–300 |

**Recipe — fastest catalog shot, studio background (20 credits):**
```json
{
  "jewelry_photo_1": "https://example.com/tennis-bracelet.jpg"
}
```

**Recipe — lifestyle social image, HQ, portrait crop (40 credits):**
```json
{
  "jewelry_photo_1": "https://example.com/bangle.jpg",
  "is_lifestyle": true,
  "user_instructions": "golden-hour café terrace, relaxed pose, warm natural light",
  "model_tier": "ViTryon PRO (HQ) - 4Mpx",
  "aspect_ratio": "4:5"
}
```

**Recipe — wrist close-up styled after the merchant's model, dainty piece (20 credits):**
```json
{
  "jewelry_photo_1": "https://example.com/chain-bracelet.jpg",
  "model_input": "https://example.com/model-bare-wrist.jpg",
  "is_closeup": true,
  "product_size": "S (Small)"
}
```

**Recipe — two-piece stack without merging the designs (20 credits):**
```json
{
  "jewelry_photo_1": "https://example.com/two-bracelets.jpg",
  "user_instructions": "the photo shows two separate bracelets; keep them as two distinct pieces and stack both together on the wrist, do not combine them into one design"
}
```

## Common failures -> cause -> fix

- **Bracelets "mixed up" / two pieces merged into one invented design** -> the source photo shows multiple bracelets and nothing disambiguates them -> add `user_instructions` explicitly stating the pieces are separate (and whether to use one or stack all), or crop the photo to the single intended bracelet and pass that URL.
- **Bracelet renders too large or too small on the wrist** -> `product_size` doesn't match the real piece, or the photo's cropping/perspective hides its proportions -> set `product_size` (XS–XL) to match and re-run; also provide a straight-on photo showing the whole piece without heavy cropping so proportions read correctly.
- **No bracelet detected** -> the image doesn't show a bracelet (or shows a watch, ring, necklace, or earrings) -> provide a clear bracelet product photo, or route to the correct app: **Watch Try-On**, **Rings Try On**, **Necklace Try - On**, **Earrings Try On**, or **Jewelry Set Try-On** for mixed sets.
- **Placement artifacts around the wrist** -> the model reference wears a watch or other bracelets on the placement wrist, or a sleeve fully covers it -> supply a reference with a bare, visible wrist, or omit `model_input` entirely.
- **Result doesn't resemble the model reference** -> expected behavior: the reference guides style only. Framing mismatches make it worse -> align `is_closeup` with the reference's framing and `is_lifestyle` with its setting; set expectations that the generated person will differ.
- **Background isn't what the reference showed** -> `is_lifestyle` contradicts the reference (studio reference with `true` adds an invented scene; lifestyle reference with `false` produces studio white) -> set the flag to match the desired background.
- **Fine detail (links, pavé, engraving) lost** -> soft or low-resolution source, or the bracelet is tiny in the frame -> pass a sharper, tighter-cropped image URL; for a worn or dull piece, run **Jewelry Retoucher Vivid** first, then try on the retouched output.
- **Dust or specks became sparkle or extra stones** -> debris in the source reads as part of the piece -> provide a photo of the cleaned bracelet, or state in `user_instructions` that the specks are dirt to be removed; check results before commercial use.
- **Piece looks changed (metal tone, charms)** -> this app never redesigns, but it reproduces what it can read — poor color/lighting in the source skews the rendering -> provide a neutrally lit photo on a plain background; for intentional design changes use **Jewelry Modifier Pro** first.

## Cost notes

- **Base: 20 credits** per run at the default `ViTryon SD - 1Mpx` tier.
- **`model_tier` is the price driver:** `ViTryon PRO (HQ) - 4Mpx` adds +20 → **40 credits**; `ViTryon PRO (HQ) - 16Mpx` adds +60 → **80 credits**.
- **Each run returns one result and is charged once**; to compare several looks, submit several runs, each charged separately (e.g. 3 runs at 4Mpx = 3 × 40 = 120 credits).
- **Discounted regeneration** of a run: 7 credits base, plus 8 at the 4Mpx tier (15 total) or 19 at the 16Mpx tier (26 total).
- Off-spec enum values are rejected before any charge. Use `estimate_run_cost` for the exact number before running.
